record.paper_title: FPT Suspects and Tough Customers: Open Problems of Downey and Fellows
record.context_brief: Directed disjoint paths in planar digraphs
record.original_question: Given a directed planar graph G and k ordered pairs of vertices ⟨r1, s1⟩, ..., ⟨rk, sk⟩, does G contain k pairwise vertex-disjoint directed paths P1, ..., Pk such that Pi runs from ri to si for each i?

evidence.quote:
Planar Directed Disjoint Paths Open
Instance: A directed planar graph G and k pairs ⟨r1,s 1⟩,..., ⟨rk,s k⟩ of
vertices ofG
Parameter: k
Question: Does G have k vertex-disjoint pathsP1,...,P k with Pi running
from ri to si?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Decision problem (parameterized by k): Given a directed planar graph G together with k ordered pairs of vertices ⟨r_1, s_1⟩, …, ⟨r_k, s_k⟩ of G, determine whether G contains k pairwise internally and externally vertex-disjoint directed paths P_1, …, P_k such that for each i ∈ {1, …, k}, P_i is a directed path from r_i to s_i. Determine whether this problem is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by k, i.e., whether it admits an algorithm running in time f(k) · n^{O(1)} for some computable function f, where n = |V(G)|.
artifact.status_search_result: Cygan, Marx, Pilipczuk, and Pilipczuk (FOCS 2013, arXiv:1304.4207) proved that the planar directed k-Vertex-Disjoint Paths problem is fixed-parameter tractable, giving an algorithm with running time 2^{2^{O(k^2)}} n^{O(1)}. This resolves the problem in the affirmative.

status_evidence.title: The planar directed k-Vertex-Disjoint Paths problem is fixed-parameter tractable
status_evidence.snippet: We show that the k-Vertex-Disjoint Paths problem on planar directed graphs is fixed-parameter tractable.
status_evidence.claim: FPT algorithm exists for planar directed k-vertex-disjoint paths.
